items.stem: A workload is a small development web server with a balanced CPU-to-memory need. Which VM size type is most appropriate?

options.rationale: Correct: general-purpose sizes provide a balanced CPU-to-memory ratio ideal for dev/test and small web servers.
GPU sizes are for graphics or AI workloads, overkill here.
HPC sizes target memory- and CPU-intensive scientific workloads.
Storage-optimised sizes target big-data and large database I/O.

items.explanation: Correct: general-purpose sizes give a balanced CPU-to-memory ratio for dev/test and small web servers.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Azure Virtual Machine cost and scaling are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Azure charges an hourly price based on size and OS, billing per minute for partial hours
options.rationale: Correct: VMs are billed by the minute for partial hours based on size and OS.

options.text: You can scale out by adding more VM instances to meet demand
options.rationale: Correct: scaling out adds instances to handle more load.

options.text: Storage for a VM is always free
options.rationale: Incorrect: storage is priced and charged separately.

options.text: A VM cannot be resized after creation
options.rationale: Incorrect: VM size can be changed after creation.

items.explanation: Correct: VMs bill per minute for partial hours and can scale out with more instances.

items.stem: What does the 'size' of an Azure Virtual Machine primarily determine?

options.text: Processing power, memory, storage capacity and network bandwidth
options.rationale: Correct: the size determines CPU, memory, storage and network characteristics.

options.text: The physical colour of the datacenter rack
options.rationale: Size is a logical specification, not a physical attribute of hardware appearance.

options.text: The Azure region the VM must run in
options.rationale: Region is chosen separately from size.
Currency is a billing account setting, not a VM size property.

items.explanation: Correct: the VM size determines processing power, memory, storage capacity and network bandwidth.
